claim: ChAdOx1 nCov-19 and Ad26.COV2.S are approved vaccines inducing protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 infection in humans by expressing the Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2.
source: ChAdOx1 nCov-19 and Ad26.COV2.S are approved vaccines inducing protective immunity against SARS-CoV-2 infection in humans by expressing the Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established fact about these vaccines.

claim: Four out of four tested lots of ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 contained significantly higher than expected levels of host cell proteins (HCPs) and of free viral proteins.
source: Four out of four tested lots of ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 contained significantly higher than expected levels of host cell proteins (HCPs) and of free viral proteins.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including SDS-PAGE, mass spectrometry, and quantification assays.

claim: The most abundant contaminating HCPs in ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 belonged to the heat-shock protein and cytoskeletal protein families.
source: The most abundant contaminating HCPs belonged to the heat-shock protein and cytoskeletal protein families.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data showing HSP 90-beta, HSP 90-alpha, and cytoskeletal proteins among the top abundant proteins.

claim: The HCP content in ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 exceeded the 400 ng specification limit per vaccine dose, as set by the European Medicines Agency (EMA), by at least 25-fold.
source: The HCP content exceeded the 400 ng specification limit per vaccine dose, as set by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for this vaccine, by at least 25-fold and the manufacturer's batch-release data in some of the lots by several hundred-fold.
evidence: This is supported by quantification data in Table 1 showing HCP amounts ranging from 9.85 to 154.53 µg per dose compared to the 0.4 µg (400 ng) specification limit.

claim: The HCP content in ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 exceeded the manufacturer's batch-release data in some of the lots by several hundred-fold.
source: The HCP content exceeded the 400 ng specification limit per vaccine dose, as set by the European Medicines Agency (EMA) for this vaccine, by at least 25-fold and the manufacturer's batch-release data in some of the lots by several hundred-fold.
evidence: This is supported by Table 1 comparing measured HCP amounts to manufacturer's batch-release data.

claim: Three tested lots of the Ad26.COV2.S vaccine contained only very low amounts of HCPs.
source: In contrast, three tested lots of the Ad26.COV2.S vaccine contained only very low amounts of HCPs.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data showing 98% of proteins in Ad26.COV2.S were of viral origin and less than 1% of human origin.

claim: Production of clinical grade adenovirus vaccines of high purity is feasible at an industrial scale, as shown for Ad26.COV2.S.
source: As shown for Ad26.COV2.S production of clinical grade adenovirus vaccines of high purity is feasible at an industrial scale.
evidence: This is inferred from the data showing Ad26.COV2.S had very low HCP contamination despite being produced at industrial scale.

claim: Purification procedures of the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine should be modified to remove protein impurities as good as possible.
source: Correspondingly, purification procedures of the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine should be modified to remove protein impurities as good as possible.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the finding of high HCP content in ChAdOx1 compared to Ad26.COV2.S.

claim: Standard quality assays, as they are used in the manufacturing of proteins, have to be adapted for vectored vaccines.
source: Our data also indicate that standard quality assays, as they are used in the manufacturing of proteins, have to be adapted for vectored vaccines.
evidence: This is inferred from the discrepancy between manufacturer's batch-release data and actual measured HCP content.

claim: The AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine (AZD1222, Vaxzevria, ChAdOx1 nCov-19) is based on Chimpanzee Adenovirus Y25.
source: The AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine (AZD1222, Vaxzevria, ChAdOx1 nCov-19 – short ChAdOx1) is based on Chimpanzee Adenovirus Y25 (Dicks et al., 2012) .
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The Johnson & Johnson Ad26.COV2.S vaccine is based on Human Adenovirus type 26 (HAdV-D26).
source: The Johnson & Johnson Ad26.COV2.S vaccine is based on Human Adenovirus type 26 (HAdV-D26) (Bos et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Both ChAdOx1 and Ad26.COV2.S vaccines express the full-length Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2.
source: Both vaccines express the full-length Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about the vaccine design.

claim: Adenovirus-based vaccines have the ability to induce potent humoral and cellular immune responses.
source: The ability of adenovirus-based vaccines to induce potent humoral and cellular immune responses and their overall safety record had made them strong candidates to successfully fight the COVID-19 pandemic.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about adenovirus-based vaccines.

claim: Billions of adenovirus-based vaccine doses have been administered to vaccinees with very low rates of serious adverse events observed.
source: This has turned out true, with billions of adenovirus-based vaccine doses administered to vaccinees and with very low rates of serious adverse events observed.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the vaccination campaign.

claim: Before the COVID-19 pandemic, adenovirus-based vaccines have not been produced at the scale required to supply billions of doses.
source: In the past, and before the COVID-19 pandemic, adenovirus-based vaccines have not been produced even close at the scale required to supply billions of doses.
evidence: This is stated as historical context about vaccine production.

claim: Scale-up of production processes in a very short period of time has been a significant challenge for all vaccines including adenovirus-based vaccines.
source: Thus, for all vaccines including for adenovirus-based vaccines scale-up of production processes in a very short period of time has been a significant challenge.
evidence: This is stated as context about the challenges of pandemic vaccine production.

claim: The ChAdOx1 vaccine is produced in human T-REx-293 cells to prevent expression of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein during vector production.
source: The vaccine is produced in human T-REx-293 cells to prevent expression of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein during vector production.
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the production process with citation support.

claim: The ChAdOx1 vaccine is purified by a combination of filtration steps and anion-exchange chromatography.
source: The vaccine is then purified by a combination of filtration steps and anion-exchange chromatography (European-Medicines-Agency, 2021a; Fedosyuk et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the purification process with citation support.

claim: Simian adenovirus vectors including ChAdOx1 can be purified at high yield and purity using filtration and anion-exchange chromatography technology.
source: Previously, it has been shown, that simian adenovirus vectors including ChAdOx1 can be purified at high yield and purity using such technology for purification (Fedosyuk et al., 2019).
evidence: This is stated as previously established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Modifications and simplifications had been introduced into the upstream and downstream processes of ChAdOx1 production to meet global needs and enable commercial manufacturing at a very large scale.
source: To meet global needs and to enable commercial manufacturing of clinical grade material at a very large scale, some modifications and simplifications, respectively, had been introduced both into the upstream and downstream processes, as has been described in detail (Joe et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as a fact about the production process with citation support.

claim: The staining pattern of ChAdOx1 looked very different compared to the HAdV-C5-EGFP adenoviral vector control when the same number of viral particles was loaded.
source: Although in our experiment the same number of viral particles was loaded, the staining pattern of ChAdOx1 looked very different, when compared to the adenoviral vector control (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by the silver-stained SDS-PAGE gel shown in Figure 1.

claim: Staining of HAdV-C5-EGFP proteins resulted in the expected band pattern, representing distinct major capsid proteins including Hexon, Penton Base, IIIa, and Fiber.
source: While staining of HAdV-C5-EGFP proteins resulted in the expected band pattern, representing distinct major capsid proteins of HAdV-C5 including Hexon, Penton Base, IIIa, and Fiber, protein staining of three different lots of ChAdOx1 showed many more bands than could be explained by proteins from viral particles.
evidence: This is supported by the silver-stained gel in Figure 1 showing the expected pattern for HAdV-C5-EGFP.

claim: Protein staining of three different lots of ChAdOx1 showed many more bands than could be explained by proteins from viral particles.
source: While staining of HAdV-C5-EGFP proteins resulted in the expected band pattern, representing distinct major capsid proteins of HAdV-C5 including Hexon, Penton Base, IIIa, and Fiber, protein staining of three different lots of ChAdOx1 showed many more bands than could be explained by proteins from viral particles.
evidence: This is supported by the silver-stained gel in Figure 1 showing multiple bands in ChAdOx1 lanes.

claim: Band intensities varied between the ChAdOx1 lots despite loading the same number of particles.
source: Additionally, despite loading the same number of particles, band intensities varied between the ChAdOx1 lots.
evidence: This is supported by visual inspection of Figure 1 showing different staining intensities across ChAdOx1 lots.

claim: ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 lots contained exclusively viral DNA, while genomic DNA of the host cell was not detected.
source: We also analyzed the ChAdOx1 nCoV-19 lots at the DNA level by quantitative polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Results confirmed the exclusive presence of viral DNA, while genomic DNA of the host cell was not detected (data not shown).
evidence: This is supported by qPCR analysis performed by the authors.

claim: In lot ABV5811, about 70% of the detected protein content was of human origin and only 30% of virus origin.
source: Based on intensity comparisons of liquid chromatography/mass spectrometry (LC/MS) signals, we estimate that in lot ABV5811 about 70% of the detected protein content was of human and only 30% of virus origin.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: In lots ABV4678 and ABV7764, approximately 50% of detected proteins were of human origin.
source: In lots ABV4678 and ABV7764 approximately 50% of detected proteins were of human origin (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Several nonstructural viral proteins were detected at high abundancy in ChAdOx1, although they are not part of the mature viral particle.
source: Beside the expected structural viral proteins forming the virion (Hexon, Penton base, IIIa, Fiber, V, VI, VII, VIII, IX, and others) also several nonstructural viral proteins were detected at high abundancy, although they are not part of the mature viral particle (Figure 2B,C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B and 2C.

claim: The 100K protein, a multifunctional scaffolding protein involved in the trimerization of Hexon, was detected among the nonstructural viral proteins.
source: To the detected nonstructural viral proteins belong, for example, the 100K protein, a multifunctional scaffolding protein involved in the trimerization of Hexon, and the DNA-binding protein, which plays an essential role in the replication of the viral genome during infection.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and established knowledge about the 100K protein function.

claim: The DNA-binding protein, which plays an essential role in the replication of the viral genome during infection, was detected among the nonstructural viral proteins.
source: To the detected nonstructural viral proteins belong, for example, the 100K protein, a multifunctional scaffolding protein involved in the trimerization of Hexon, and the DNA-binding protein, which plays an essential role in the replication of the viral genome during infection.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data and established knowledge about the DNA-binding protein function.

claim: In lot ABV5811, nonstructural proteins represented 30% of detected adenoviral proteins.
source: In lot ABV5811 nonstructural proteins represented 30% of detected adenoviral proteins (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: In the vaccine product, significant amounts of structural proteins were present as monomers, oligomers, or incomplete viral capsid assemblies.
source: Since in the assembly process during virus propagation only a part of the available viral capsid proteins is used for particle formation, we assume that in the vaccine product also significant amounts of structural proteins were present as monomers, oligomers, or incomplete viral capsid assemblies.
evidence: This is inferred from the detection of high amounts of structural proteins and knowledge of virus assembly processes.

claim: Both nonstructural viral proteins and nonencapsidated structural proteins are referred to as product-related impurities.
source: Not being part of the mature viral particle, both nonstructural viral proteins and nonencapsidated structural proteins are referred to as product-related impurities.
evidence: This is a definition provided by the authors based on standard terminology.

claim: Peptides from more than 1000 different human proteins, derived from the human production cell line, were detected in ChAdOx1.
source: Peptides from more than 1000 different human proteins, derived from the human production cell line, were detected (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: The detected human proteins were derived from different cellular compartments including cytoplasm, nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and others.
source: They were derived from different cellular compartments including cytoplasm, nucleus, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, and others.
evidence: This is based on analysis of the mass spectrometry data identifying proteins from various cellular compartments.

claim: Relative amounts of human versus viral proteins were variable between ChAdOx1 lots.
source: Relative amounts of human versus viral proteins were variable between lots (Figure 2A), as was already assumed based on the silver-stained gels (Figure 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data in Figure 2A and SDS-PAGE in Figure 1.

claim: Among the human proteins found in the ChAdOx1 vaccine, the group of heat-shock proteins (HSPs) and chaperones stood out in abundancy.
source: Among the human proteins found in the vaccine and beside several cytoskeletal proteins including Vimentin, Tubulin, Actin, and Actinin, the group of heat-shock proteins (HSPs) and chaperones stood out in abundancy.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data showing HSPs among the top abundant proteins.

claim: HSP 90-beta and HSP 90-alpha as cytosolic HSPs were present at 9.5% and 4.3% of the total proteins, respectively, in ChAdOx1 lot ABV5811.
source: Among the top abundant proteins, HSP 90-beta and HSP 90-alpha as cytosolic HSPs (9.5% and 4.3% of the total proteins, respectively) and three chaperones of the endoplasmic reticulum (transitional endoplasmic reticulum ATPase, Endoplasmin, and Calreticulin) were present (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Three chaperones of the endoplasmic reticulum (transitional endoplasmic reticulum ATPase, Endoplasmin, and Calreticulin) were present among the top abundant proteins in ChAdOx1.
source: Among the top abundant proteins, HSP 90-beta and HSP 90-alpha as cytosolic HSPs (9.5% and 4.3% of the total proteins, respectively) and three chaperones of the endoplasmic reticulum (transitional endoplasmic reticulum ATPase, Endoplasmin, and Calreticulin) were present (Figure 2C and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Proteins from Bos taurus from fetal calf serum used for growth of T-REx-293 producer cells were detected at low or negligible levels in ChAdOx1.
source: Proteins from Bos taurus from fetal calf serum used for growth of T-REx-293 producer cells, Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 and T-Rex-293 cell-derived proteins (E1B from HAdV-C5, Tet-Repressor) were detected at low or negligible levels (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 was detected at low or negligible levels in ChAdOx1.
source: Proteins from Bos taurus from fetal calf serum used for growth of T-REx-293 producer cells, Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 and T-Rex-293 cell-derived proteins (E1B from HAdV-C5, Tet-Repressor) were detected at low or negligible levels (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: T-Rex-293 cell-derived proteins (E1B from HAdV-C5, Tet-Repressor) were detected at low or negligible levels in ChAdOx1.
source: Proteins from Bos taurus from fetal calf serum used for growth of T-REx-293 producer cells, Spike protein of SARS-CoV-2 and T-Rex-293 cell-derived proteins (E1B from HAdV-C5, Tet-Repressor) were detected at low or negligible levels (Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data.

claim: Ad26.COV2.S is purified using filtration and chromatography steps.
source: A second approved adenoviral vaccine, based on HAdV-D26, is also purified using filtration and chromatography steps (European-Medicines-Agency, 2021b).
evidence: This is stated with citation support from regulatory documents.

claim: There was very little protein contamination in Ad26.COV2.S compared to ChAdOx1.
source: We compared again a CsCl-purified HAdV-C5-EGFP adenovirus vector with three lots of Ad26.COV2.S (lots 21C10-01, XD955, XE395) and a further (fourth) lot of ChAdOx1 (ABV9317) (Figure 3) and found very little protein contamination in Ad26.COV2.S compared to ChAdOx1 (Figure 3A-C and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by SDS-PAGE and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3.

claim: More than 93% of proteins detected in HAdV-C5-EGFP were of HAdV-C5 origin.
source: Mass spectrometry confirmed that more than 93% of proteins detected in HAdV-C5-EGFP were of HAdV-C5 origin (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: 98% of proteins detected in Ad26.COV2.S (lot XD955) were of HAdV-D26 origin and less than 1% of human origin.
source: Furthermore, 98% of proteins detected in Ad26.COV2.S (lot XD955) were of HAdV-D26 and less than 1% of human origin.
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: In lot ABV9317 of ChAdOx1, 70% of proteins were of human origin and only 30% of adenovirus origin.
source: In contrast, in lot ABV9317 of ChAdOx1 70% of proteins were of human and only 30% of adenovirus origin (Figure 3B,C and Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Viral structural to nonstructural protein ratios were 92% versus 8% in Ad26.COV2.S.
source: Determination of structural and nonstructural viral proteins revealed viral structural to nonstructural protein ratios of 92% versus 8% and of 70% versus 30% in Ad26.COV2.S compared to ChAdOx1, respectively (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Viral structural to nonstructural protein ratios were 70% versus 30% in ChAdOx1.
source: Determination of structural and nonstructural viral proteins revealed viral structural to nonstructural protein ratios of 92% versus 8% and of 70% versus 30% in Ad26.COV2.S compared to ChAdOx1, respectively (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The top human host cell proteins in Ad26.COV2.S were histones and ribosomal proteins, rather than the HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins found in ChAdOx1.
source: The top human host cell proteins (HCPs) in Ad26.COV2.S, although present only at very low abundancy, were histones and ribosomal proteins, rather than the HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins found in ChAdOx1 (Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry data comparing the protein profiles of the two vaccines.

claim: According to European Medicines Agency (EMA) quality specifications for ChAdOx1, 400 ng is the maximally allowable HCP content per single dose (5 × 10^10 vector particles).
source: According to European Medicines Agency (EMA) quality specifications for ChAdOx1, 400 ng is the maximally allowable HCP content per single dose (5 × 1010 vector particles).
evidence: This is stated as a regulatory specification.

claim: Three standard methods were used to determine the HCP content in the tested ChAdOx1 lots: NanoDrop absorbance at 280 nm, Bradford assay, and ImageJ analysis.
source: Since the quantification of total protein amounts in inhomogeneous protein mixtures is inherently afflicted with uncertainty due to differences in biophysical properties of the individual proteins, we used three standard methods to determine the HCP content in the tested ChAdOx1 lots (Table 1).
evidence: This is stated in the methods and results sections describing the experimental approach.

claim: 12.8 µg virus protein is contained in 5 × 10^10 vector particles.
source: We took into account the 12.8 µg protein amount contained in 5 × 1010 vector particles, that can be calculated based on the known 150 MDa molecular weight of adenovirus particles (Sweeney and Hennessey, 2002).
evidence: This is calculated based on the known molecular weight of adenovirus particles with citation support.

claim: Total protein contents in ChAdOx1 varied with the method used for analysis.
source: As expected, and as apparent from Table 1, total protein contents varied with the method used for analysis.
evidence: This is supported by the different values obtained from the three methods shown in Table 1.

claim: Independent of the method used, protein amounts contained in the ChAdOx1 vaccine significantly exceeded the 400 ng specification limit by a factor of 25 or higher.
source: However, independent of the method used and as already expected from inspection of Figure 3A, protein amounts contained in the vaccine significantly exceeded the 400 ng specification limit by a factor of 25 or higher, and the manufacturer's batch-release data by an even much larger (several hundred-fold) extent.
evidence: This is supported by the quantification data in Table 1 showing HCP amounts ranging from 9.85 to 154.53 µg per dose.

claim: UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19 was purified to more than 90% purity by standard CsCl density gradient ultracentrifugation.
source: We amplified ChAdOx1 nCov-19 in HEK293T cells and purified this vector to more than 90% purity (renamed UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19) by standard CsCl density gradient ultracentrifugation (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by SDS-PAGE and mass spectrometry data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: T-cell responses (against one tested T-cell epitope) were 1.3-fold lower after vaccination using UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19 compared to vaccination using AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19.
source: T-cell responses (against one tested T-cell epitope) were 1.3-fold lower after vaccination using UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19 compared to vaccination using AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19.
evidence: This is supported by the T-cell response data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Total antibody titers were 1.3-fold lower after vaccination using UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19 compared to vaccination using AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19.
source: Similarly, total antibody titers were also 1.3-fold lower after vaccination using UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19 compared to vaccination using AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19.
evidence: This is supported by the antibody titer data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Differences in T-cell responses and antibody titers between AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19 and UUlm ChAdOx1 nCov-19 were not statistically significant.
source: However, differences between the two groups were not statistically significant in both parameters, indicating that in this limited study performed in mice there was no indication for obvious interference in induced immune responses related to the HCPs in the original AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine.
evidence: This is supported by the statistical analysis of the data shown in Figure 4B and 4C.

claim: In the limited study performed in mice, there was no indication for obvious interference in induced immune responses related to the HCPs in the original AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine.
source: However, differences between the two groups were not statistically significant in both parameters, indicating that in this limited study performed in mice there was no indication for obvious interference in induced immune responses related to the HCPs in the original AstraZeneca ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of statistically significant differences in immune responses between the two vaccine preparations.

claim: HSPs and chaperones found at substantial levels in the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine are equipped with ATPase activity.
source: Since HSPs and chaperones, found at substantial levels in the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine are equipped with ATPase activity and because ADP is a strong activator of platelets, we analyzed, whether ATPase activity was detectable in the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about HSPs and chaperones.

claim: ADP is a strong activator of platelets.
source: Since HSPs and chaperones, found at substantial levels in the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine are equipped with ATPase activity and because ADP is a strong activator of platelets, we analyzed, whether ATPase activity was detectable in the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about ADP.

claim: ATPase activity was detectable in the ChAdOx1 nCov-19 vaccine.
source: Results confirmed the presence of ATPase activity in the vaccine (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: This is supported by the ATPase activity assay data shown in Figure 5.

claim: The HCP content in ChAdOx1 exceeded the manufacturer's batch-release data by an even much larger (several hundred-fold) extent.
source: However, independent of the method used and as already expected from inspection of Figure 3A, protein amounts contained in the vaccine significantly exceeded the 400 ng specification limit by a factor of 25 or higher, and the manufacturer's batch-release data by an even much larger (several hundred-fold) extent.
evidence: This is supported by comparing the measured HCP amounts in Table 1 to the manufacturer's batch-release data.

claim: The substantial lot-to-lot variation in HCP content in four tested ChAdOx1 samples indicated a lack of robustness of the process used for purification of the vaccine.
source: The substantial lot-to-lot variation in HCP content in a total of four tested samples (Figure 1 and Table 1) also indicated a lack of robustness of the process used for purification of the vaccine, a process, which recently has been described in detail (Joe et al., 2022).
evidence: This is inferred from the observed variation in HCP content across different lots.

claim: The vast majority of the more than 1000 different proteins detected in ChAdOx1 will not cause any adverse effects.
source: One can assume that the vast majority of the more than 1000 different proteins detected, most of which present at low abundancy, will not cause any adverse effects.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the low abundance of most detected proteins.

claim: The most abundant proteins in ChAdOx1 do not belong to the group of 'high risk' HCPs such as cytokines, proteases, and lipases.
source: We note that the most abundant proteins do not belong to the group of 'high risk' HCPs such as cytokines, proteases, and lipases, as they have been described in the context of protein therapeutics (Jones et al., 2021).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the mass spectrometry data and comparison to known high-risk HCPs with citation support.

claim: Extracellular HSPs are known to modulate innate and adaptive immune responses.
source: For example, extracellular HSPs are known to modulate innate and adaptive immune responses, can exacerbate preexisting inflammatory condition, have been associated with autoimmunity and can even become targets auf autoimmune responses themselves (Binder, 2014; Routsias and Tzioufas, 2006; Tamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Extracellular HSPs can exacerbate preexisting inflammatory condition.
source: For example, extracellular HSPs are known to modulate innate and adaptive immune responses, can exacerbate preexisting inflammatory condition, have been associated with autoimmunity and can even become targets auf autoimmune responses themselves (Binder, 2014; Routsias and Tzioufas, 2006; Tamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Extracellular HSPs have been associated with autoimmunity.
source: For example, extracellular HSPs are known to modulate innate and adaptive immune responses, can exacerbate preexisting inflammatory condition, have been associated with autoimmunity and can even become targets auf autoimmune responses themselves (Binder, 2014; Routsias and Tzioufas, 2006; Tamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Extracellular HSPs can become targets of autoimmune responses themselves.
source: For example, extracellular HSPs are known to modulate innate and adaptive immune responses, can exacerbate preexisting inflammatory condition, have been associated with autoimmunity and can even become targets auf autoimmune responses themselves (Binder, 2014; Routsias and Tzioufas, 2006; Tamura et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: HSPs very efficiently initiate specific immune responses by receptor-mediated uptake of HSP–peptide complexes in antigen-presenting cells (APCs), mainly via CD91 and scavenger receptors.
source: They very efficiently initiate specific immune responses by receptor-mediated uptake of HSP–peptide complexes in antigen-presenting cells (APCs), mainly via CD91 and scavenger receptors (Binder, 2014; Binder et al., 2000).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: HSPs present in the vaccine could mediate the transfer to APCs of peptides derived from the 293 cell source, of autologous peptides from vaccinated individuals, and also of viral proteins.
source: Since the HSPs present in the vaccine are derived from T-REx-293 cells, in principle they could mediate the transfer to APCs of peptides derived from the 293 cell source, of autologous peptides from vaccinated individuals and also of viral proteins.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the known function of HSPs and their presence in the vaccine.

claim: Adenovirus has been reported to induce HSPs during amplification in production cells.
source: Like many viruses, adenovirus has been reported to induce HSPs during amplification in production cells (Santoro et al., 2010), likely to accommodate for a need in help by HSPs in the folding and production of large amounts of structural and nonstructural viral proteins and in virion assembly.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Virus infection-mediated induction of HSPs could explain the abundancy of HSPs in the vaccine product in case of insufficient purification.
source: Thus, virus infection-mediated induction of HSPs could explain the abundancy of HSPs in the vaccine product in case of insufficient purification.
evidence: This is inferred from the known induction of HSPs by adenovirus and the detection of high HSP levels in the vaccine.

claim: Local ADP generation in the ATP-rich skeletal muscle tissue after injection might contribute to activation of platelets following ADP receptor binding.
source: Because HSPs are endowed with ATPase activity, we searched for and detected ATPase activity in ChAdOx1 (Figure 5), raising the possibility that local ADP generation in the ATP-rich skeletal muscle tissue after injection might contribute to activation of platelets following ADP receptor binding.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the detection of ATPase activity in the vaccine.

claim: Cases of thrombotic thrombocytopenia were observed shortly after ChAdOx1 received conditional marketing authorization in Europe.
source: Shortly after receiving conditional marketing authorization in Europe, cases of thrombotic thrombocytopenia were observed, an unusual and, if untreated, often fatal syndrome of thrombosis of the cerebral venous sinuses and other large vessels together with low platelet counts.
evidence: This is stated as an observed clinical phenomenon.

claim: Thrombotic thrombocytopenia is an unusual and, if untreated, often fatal syndrome of thrombosis of the cerebral venous sinuses and other large vessels together with low platelet counts.
source: Shortly after receiving conditional marketing authorization in Europe, cases of thrombotic thrombocytopenia were observed, an unusual and, if untreated, often fatal syndrome of thrombosis of the cerebral venous sinuses and other large vessels together with low platelet counts.
evidence: This is stated as a medical definition.

claim: Thrombotic thrombocytopenia occurs between 5 and 28 days after vaccination.
source: Occurring between 5 and 28 days after vaccination (Othman et al., 2021), this syndrome, now coined vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) or thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and related to autoimmune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (Greinacher et al., 2017), was found to be linked to vaccination with ChAdOx1 (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021), and has been described to be mediated by platelet-activating antibodies against platelet factor 4 (PF4) (Greinacher et al., 2021a ; Greinacher et al., 2021b; Pavord et al., 2021; Schultz et al., 2021; Scully et al., 2021; Tiede et al., 2021; Wolf et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observed clinical characteristic with citation support.

claim: Vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) is related to autoimmune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
source: Occurring between 5 and 28 days after vaccination (Othman et al., 2021), this syndrome, now coined vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) or thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and related to autoimmune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (Greinacher et al., 2017), was found to be linked to vaccination with ChAdOx1 (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021), and has been described to be mediated by platelet-activating antibodies against platelet factor 4 (PF4) (Greinacher et al., 2021a ; Greinacher et al., 2021b; Pavord et al., 2021; Schultz et al., 2021; Scully et al., 2021; Tiede et al., 2021; Wolf et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: VITT was found to be linked to vaccination with ChAdOx1.
source: Occurring between 5 and 28 days after vaccination (Othman et al., 2021), this syndrome, now coined vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) or thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and related to autoimmune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (Greinacher et al., 2017), was found to be linked to vaccination with ChAdOx1 (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021), and has been described to be mediated by platelet-activating antibodies against platelet factor 4 (PF4) (Greinacher et al., 2021a ; Greinacher et al., 2021b; Pavord et al., 2021; Schultz et al., 2021; Scully et al., 2021; Tiede et al., 2021; Wolf et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observed association with citation support.

claim: VITT has been described to be mediated by platelet-activating antibodies against platelet factor 4 (PF4).
source: Occurring between 5 and 28 days after vaccination (Othman et al., 2021), this syndrome, now coined vaccine-induced immune thrombotic thrombocytopenia (VITT) or thrombosis with thrombocytopenia syndrome, and related to autoimmune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (Greinacher et al., 2017), was found to be linked to vaccination with ChAdOx1 (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021), and has been described to be mediated by platelet-activating antibodies against platelet factor 4 (PF4) (Greinacher et al., 2021a ; Greinacher et al., 2021b; Pavord et al., 2021; Schultz et al., 2021; Scully et al., 2021; Tiede et al., 2021; Wolf et al., 2021).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with multiple citation support.

claim: Ad26.COV2.S has been linked to VITT, however at a lower frequency than ChAdOx1.
source: Also Ad26.COV2.S has been linked to VITT (Muir et al., 2021; Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021), however at a lower frequency (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2022).
evidence: This is stated as an observed association with citation support.

claim: It has been speculated that impurities in ChAdOx1 could be causally involved in the pathogenesis of VITT.
source: It has recently been speculated that impurities in ChAdOx1 could be causally involved in the pathogenesis of VITT (Greinacher et al., 2021a).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation from the literature with citation support.

claim: The findings support the notion that the protein impurities present in ChAdOx1 at least are not the primary trigger for the induction of VITT.
source: Since VITT has been found associated with both ChAdOx1 and Ad26.COV2.S, at a lower frequency in the latter (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021), and because, according to our data, ChAdOx1 but not Ad26.COV2.S contained high amounts of human and free viral proteins, our findings support the notion that the protein impurities present in ChAdOx1 at least are not the primary trigger for the induction of VITT.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both vaccines are associated with VITT despite different HCP content.

claim: PF4 itself was not found as a contaminant in the ChAdOx1 analyses.
source: Incidentally, PF4 itself was not found in our analyses as a contaminant.
evidence: This is stated as a negative finding from the mass spectrometry analyses.

claim: The impurities in ChAdOx1 might increase the likelihood and frequency of VITT occurrence by serving as an inflammatory or immunological cofactor.
source: Whether the impurities might increase the likelihood and frequency of its occurrence in case of ChAdOx1, for example by serving as an inflammatory or immunological cofactor remains a possibility.
evidence: This is stated as a speculative possibility.

claim: Epidemiologic studies have indicated that RNA vaccines are associated with thromboembolic events but not with VITT.
source: Interestingly, epidemiologic studies have indicated that RNA vaccines are associated with thromboembolic events but not with VITT (Paul-Ehrlich-Institut, 2021).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from epidemiologic studies with citation support.

claim: Differences in duration and/or levels of Spike protein expression between adenoviral vectors and mRNA vaccines might be a relevant factor in the pathogenesis of VITT.
source: We speculate that differences in duration and/or levels of Spike protein expression, as to be expected in adenoviral vectors versus mRNA vaccines, might also be a relevant factor in the pathogenesis of VITT, as well as the secretion of the Spike protein due to aberrant splicing events, as recently observed with adenovirus-based vaccines, more so with ChAdOx1 than with Ad26.COV2.S (Kowarz et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation with citation support for the aberrant splicing observation.

claim: Secretion of the Spike protein due to aberrant splicing events has been observed with adenovirus-based vaccines, more so with ChAdOx1 than with Ad26.COV2.S.
source: We speculate that differences in duration and/or levels of Spike protein expression, as to be expected in adenoviral vectors versus mRNA vaccines, might also be a relevant factor in the pathogenesis of VITT, as well as the secretion of the Spike protein due to aberrant splicing events, as recently observed with adenovirus-based vaccines, more so with ChAdOx1 than with Ad26.COV2.S (Kowarz et al., 2022).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the literature with citation support.

claim: The frequency of severe thromboembolic events occurring after natural infection with SARS-CoV-2 is much higher than after vaccination with any of the vaccines in use including ChAdOx1 and Ad26.COV2.S.
source: However, it is important to stress that the frequency of severe thromboembolic events occurring after natural infection with SARS-CoV-2 is much higher than after vaccination with any of the vaccines in use including ChAdOx1 and Ad26.COV2.S (Lau et al., 2021; Nopp et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated as an important context with citation support.

claim: In a pilot in vivo immunization experiment performed in mice, anti-Spike antibody and T-cell responses were not significantly altered following immunization with ChAdOx1 compared to an identical vector without HCP contamination.
source: In a pilot in vivo immunization experiment performed in mice, anti-Spike antibody and T-cell responses were not significantly altered following immunization with ChAdOx1 compared to an identical vector without HCP contamination (Figure 4), suggesting that the protein impurities did not interfere with the induction of immune responses against the Spike antigen.
evidence: This is supported by the immunization data shown in Figure 4.

claim: The protein impurities in ChAdOx1 did not interfere with the induction of immune responses against the Spike antigen in mice.
source: In a pilot in vivo immunization experiment performed in mice, anti-Spike antibody and T-cell responses were not significantly altered following immunization with ChAdOx1 compared to an identical vector without HCP contamination (Figure 4), suggesting that the protein impurities did not interfere with the induction of immune responses against the Spike antigen.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of significant differences in immune responses between the two vaccine preparations in mice.

claim: In the biopharmaceutical industry, the removal of HCPs from the biological product is a critical quality attribute.
source: In the biopharmaceutical industry, the removal of HCPs from the biological product is a critical quality attribute, since residual HCPs pose a risk to patient safety (Vanderlaan et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2009; Zhu-Shimoni et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the biopharmaceutical industry with citation support.

claim: Residual HCPs pose a risk to patient safety.
source: In the biopharmaceutical industry, the removal of HCPs from the biological product is a critical quality attribute, since residual HCPs pose a risk to patient safety (Vanderlaan et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2009; Zhu-Shimoni et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: The main risks of HCPs relate to the biological activity of the contaminant, to effects of the impurities enhancing immune responses against the therapeutic protein (antidrug antibodies), or to inducing antibodies against the impurities.
source: The main risks generally discussed relate either to the biological activity of the contaminant, to effects of the impurities enhancing immune responses against the therapeutic protein (antidrug antibodies) or to inducing antibodies against the impurities (Vanderlaan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: Classical protein biopharmaceuticals have an excellent safety record.
source: Overall, problems with HCPs are rare events and classical protein biopharmaceuticals have an excellent safety record (de Zafra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation support.

claim: In cases where problems with HCPs have been observed, therapeutic proteins have been produced in heterologous (i.e., nonhuman) production systems such as E. coli, yeast, and Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell lines.
source: In cases, in which problems have been observed, therapeutic proteins have been produced in heterologous (i.e., nonhuman) production systems such as E. coli, yeast, and Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cell lines (de Zafra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the literature with citation support.

claim: Antidrug antibodies were generated in patients against human growth hormone produced in E. coli, apparently due to a contaminating protein that had been missed by an unsuitable HCP assay.
source: For example, antidrug antibodies were generated in patients against human growth hormone (Vanderlaan et al., 2018), produced in E. coli, apparently due to a contaminating protein that had been missed by an unsuitable HCP assay.
evidence: This is stated as an example from the literature with citation support.

claim: Bovine neonatal pancytopenia is a severe vaccine-induced alloimmune disease in young calves that is caused by alloreactive maternal antibodies present in the colostrum of cows that had been vaccinated against bovine viral diarrhea.
source: Another case, more closely related to the topic of this report, is bovine neonatal pancytopenia, a severe vaccine-induce alloimmune disease in young calves that is caused by alloreactive maternal antibodies present in the colostrum of cows that had been vaccinated against bovine viral diarrhea (Kasonta et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an example from the literature with citation support.

claim: Bioprocess impurities in the bovine viral diarrhea vaccine, originating from the bovine production cell line, induced alloreactive antibodies directed to polymorphic bovine leukocyte antigen I (BoLA class I) alleles.
source: Bioprocess impurities in the vaccine, originating from the bovine i.e. autologous, production cell line, used for virus propagation and vaccine production, induced these alloreactive antibodies present in the colostrum of vaccinated cows that were directed to polymorphic bovine leukocyte antigen I (BoLA class I) alleles and became symptomatic in the offspring (Kasonta et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as an explanation from the literature with citation support.

claim: For biopharmaceuticals used in humans, one can expect lower immune-related risks linked to HCP impurities when they are produced in human cell lines.
source: In principle, for biopharmaceuticals used in humans one can expect lower immune-related risks linked to HCP impurities when they are produced in human cell lines (de Zafra et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a general principle with citation support.

claim: Guidance documents by the US Pharmacopeia (USP) and the European Pharmacopeia emphasize that HCP impurities should be as low as technically feasible.
source: Guidance documents by the US Pharmacopeia (USP) and the European Pharmacopeia emphasize that HCP impurities should be as low as technically feasible (Vanderlaan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as regulatory guidance with citation support.

claim: For 'classical' biopharmaceuticals such as antibodies, the allowable HCP content generally is in a range of 1–100 parts per million (1–100 ppm), corresponding to 1–100 ng HCP in 1 mg product.
source: For 'classical' biopharmaceuticals such as antibodies the allowable HCP content generally is in a range of 1–100 parts per million (1–100 ppm), corresponding to 1–100 ng HCP in 1 mg product (Wang et al., 2009; Vanderlaan et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a standard specification with citation support.

claim: The HCP content in more complex biotherapeutics such as viral vectors will be higher than in protein therapeutics, since production processes are more demanding.
source: The HCP content in more complex biotherapeutics such as viral vectors will be higher than in protein therapeutics, since production processes are more demanding.
evidence: This is stated as a general principle about viral vector production.

claim: HCP specifications for viral vectors are individually determined by the regulatory bodies.
source: Therefore, HCP specifications are individually determined by the regulatory bodies.
evidence: This is stated as a regulatory practice.

claim: One of the likely reasons why the specification limit of 400 ng HCP content per dose was largely exceeded in ChAdOx1 has to do with the assays used for HCP determination in the purified product.
source: One of the likely reasons, why in the case of ChAdOx1 the specification limit of 400 ng HCP content per dose was largely exceeded (Table 1), has to do with the assays used for HCP determination in the purified product.
evidence: This is inferred from the discussion of ELISA limitations.

claim: Standard assays to monitor removal of HCPs during production of biopharmaceuticals are enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs), based on polyclonal antibodies isolated from larger animals after immunization with cell lysates or supernatants from the producer cell.
source: Standard assays to monitor removal of HCPs during production of biopharmaceuticals are enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays (ELISAs) (Wang et al., 2009; Vanderlaan et al., 2018; European Directorate for the Quality of Medicine and Health Care, 2020), based on polyclonal antibodies isolated from larger animals, preferentially goat, sheep, and rabbit, after immunization with cell lysates or supernatants from the producer cell.
evidence: This is stated as standard practice with citation support.

claim: The apparent lack of detection by the manufacturer of HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins in ChAdOx1 with an ELISA could be explained by the close to 100% homology at the protein level of HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins between human and sheep or goat.
source: The apparent lack of detection by the manufacturer of HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins in ChAdOx1 with an ELISA could be explained by the close to 100% homology at the protein level of HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins between human and sheep or goat, so that in immunized animals no or low-level antibodies against these protein classes were generated.
evidence: This is inferred as an explanation for the discrepancy between manufacturer's data and actual measurements.

claim: HSPs and cytoskeletal proteins could be missed if quality control was solely based on a polyclonal ELISA, particularly if not complemented by orthogonal analytical methods such as staining of protein gels, capillary electrophoresis, or mass spectrometry.
source: Thereby, these proteins could be missed, if quality control was solely based on such a polyclonal ELISA, in particular, if it was not complemented by orthogonal analytical methods such as staining of protein gels, capillary electrophoresis, or mass spectrometry.
evidence: This is inferred from the limitations of ELISA-based detection.

claim: It will be necessary to reduce the level of contamination with process- and product-related impurities in ChAdOx1 by an improved purification process to reduce potential risks as good as possible.
source: In order to reduce potential risks as good as possible it will be necessary to reduce the level of contamination with process- and product-related impurities by an improved purification process.
evidence: This is a recommendation based on the findings of high impurity levels.

claim: The establishment of robust assays for detection of HCPs can be complicated and time consuming.
source: The establishment of robust assays for detection of HCPs can be complicated and time consuming (Wang et al., 2009), in particular if processes for new and complex biopharmaceuticals have to be developed, time that maybe is not always available in times of a pandemic.
evidence: This is stated as a general challenge with citation support.

claim: The identification of specific process- and product-related impurities in ChAdOx1 should guide and accelerate the next steps to improve purity and quality of this and similar vaccines in the future.
source: However, the here reported identification of specific process- and product-related impurities in ChAdOx1 should guide and accelerate the next steps to improve purity and quality of this and similar vaccines in the future.
evidence: This is stated as an expected outcome of the study.
